items.source: А кто не пьет, назови, нет, я жду!
items.reference: And who doesn't drink? Pray, tell me, name them!! Go on, I'll wait!

general.text: Эта реплика иллюстрирует склонность артиста Велюрова к сценической самопрезентации и высокопарной самодраматизации даже в моменты бытовых телефонных оправданий. Фраза стала универсальным культурным мемом для комичной защиты собственных слабостей и пороков.

items.candidate:
Who doesn't drink? Name one!
No, I'm waiting.

issues.justification: The mock-theatrical self-dramatization of the source ('назови, нет, я жду!') is flattened. 'Pray, tell me' and 'Go on, I'll wait!' carry the histrionic tone the analysis describes, while 'No, I'm waiting.' reads as a plain statement and weakens the comic self-presentation.

items.source: А не хлопнуть ли нам по рюмашке?
items.reference: Shall we toss back a quick one?

general.text: Этот вопрос идеально передает сюжетную функцию Костика как молодого трикстера, провокатора и медиатора в коммунальной квартире. Пассаж примечателен тем, что мгновенно и с иронией снижает патетику предыдущего монолога Велюрова, переводя высокую драму в регистр простого бытового товарищества.

items.candidate: shall we have a little drink?

issues.justification: 'have a little drink' is blander than the colloquial, slightly playful register of 'не хлопнуть ли нам по рюмашке?'. The analysis stresses the casual camaraderie and the sharp tonal drop after Velyurov's monologue, which the candidate only partly conveys.
The candidate starts with a lowercase letter, which is inconsistent with standard subtitle capitalization and makes the line look unfinished compared with the reference.

items.reference: What an evolved... highly e-v-volved relationship!

general.text: Одна из самых узнаваемых цитат фильма, функционирующая как повторяющийся рефрен. Она саркастически резюмирует нелепость тройственного союза Маргариты Павловны, Саввы и Хоботова, блестяще подчеркивая комический контраст между заявляемой интеллигентностью и реальным удушающим контролем.

eng.nb: using a literal noun-phrase structure (like "High relations!") instead of a natural exclamatory phrase.

items.candidate:
Such elevated... elevated relations.
You'll beg from door to door,
driven by cruel fate...
Tormented by wounds of the soul,
you'll long for death.
- Is that Camões?
- No, François Villon.
- It's from his testament.
- Did he die too?
Yes. He was either murdered
or hanged.
Goodness... Is that what happens
to every poet?
Nearly every one.
Listen, Lev Yevgenyevich,
the Orloviches are here.
Alas...
- Come on, don't start.
- I'm telling you, I can't.
But she said you absolutely
had to come.
But I'm busy.
That's not right.
She told you this morning.
And this morning I said I couldn't.
Sorry, Savva, but this is absurd.
- You're not coming?
- No, I'm not.
Shall I tell her that?
Tell her.
You'll upset Margarita Pavlovna.
- I regret that.
- It's not right.
How wonderful. Thanks to you,
I've realized I mustn't be afraid to live.
- What is there to fear?
- Nor should I put things off.
Buried in stony ditches,
we shall never return, alas...
- Is that François...?
- No, Rimbaud. Arthur Rimbaud.
He died in the nineteenth century.
Very gifted, very unhappy.
- Him too?
- Yes. They amputated his leg.
Oh! They all seem to have agreed
on it.
You're right. There is some mystery...
Oh, your lips are trembling.
Shall I teach you a little polka?
You dance?
No, it's an old French song,
very innocent and very clear.
I'll sing it for you.
Rosa Munda, we've reached
the end of the road.
Rosa Munda, there's nothing
for us here.
Rosa Munda, my hometown
waits for me.
Time to say goodbye, Rosa Munda;
we're going home.
We'll wear neckties again.
Go home without asking for leave.
- He's quite distinctive, isn't he?
- Yes, there's something genuine in him.
We'll meet girls
and walk them home at dawn.
Rosa Munda, schenkt mir
das Herz und die...
Rosa Munda, frag du nicht
mehr die Mama...
Rosa Munda, glaub mir,
ärg're dich nicht...
Well, what's going on in there?
- They're playing at being French.
- Yes, art still has much to answer for.
When will you be back?
I don't know, my angel.
Nights, as a rule,
are full of surprises, aren't they?
I warn you, one day
your Kostik will surprise you.
Arkady Varlamovich,
why aren't you watching the film?
You're a servant of the Muses.
I serve Mosestrada.
Mon papa ne veut pas
que je danse, que je danse!
How wonderful!
- Charming, isn't it?
- Yes!
Someone's knocking.
They're knocking!
Knocking.
- What is all this supposed to mean?
- Well...
The Orloviches are waiting.
Forgive me, but what does that
have to do with me now?
That's petty, Khobotov!
You know I could never stand them.
You're blinded by your prejudices.
I'm sorry, I have no time
to argue. I have a guest.
- Oh? How many?
- That's beside the point.
Velyurov said something.
She's some sort of nursery teacher.
Velyurov's a gossip.
Besides, it's no one's business.
- Oh, I see! You have a rendezvous?
- Enough, Margo. Please.
What does she see in you?
For all your childishness,
you're far too big...
for a nursery.
For one thing, she's a medical worker.
- And I'm a grown man.
- You're grown up?
- Without Savva and me, you'd perish.
- Who knows?
- You poor enfant terrible.
- No, no, no!
Don't make a scene, Khobotov.
- Well, hello!
- Hello.
- If I'm not mistaken... Raisa?
- Lyudmila.
Yes... That's what I thought.
Now, dear, I wanted to tell you...
Her name is Lyudochka,
not "dear."
My name is Margarita Pavlovna.
Until recently, I was...
Lev Yevgenyevich's wife.
We're no longer married,
but we remain family.
So it's only natural
that I take his interests to heart.
Please, Margo.
But that's not the point right now.
You see, Lev Yevgenyevich
has his little eccentricities.
He can't concentrate.
He knows guests are coming tonight,
yet casually invites you over.
Yes, yes. I'll leave.
Lyudochka...
You're very absent-minded!
Goodbye, dear!
"Dear"! Lyudochka!
This is unbearable!
- Khobotov, you're ridiculous.
- Why?
Why am I ridiculous?
Suppose I've fallen in love.
You, in love?
You're incapable of it, like all closet erotomaniacs.
I repeat: if you meet a woman
who inspires my confidence...
and to whom I can entrust you
with a clear conscience, I'll be happy.
Come on, get up. Let's go.
It's embarrassing in front of the Orloviches.
Turn around now.
There's no reason for them to think
that our family, too, suffers...
these petty domestic upheavals.
Oh... Lyova's here.
Whether you're happy
or trouble has found you,
amid the humming crowd,
I've long been walking
toward you.
Amid the humming crowd,
I sing of you, and hope, and wait.
One burin isn't like another.
A pointed burin is one thing.
A round burin is quite another.
I can't agree.
There's more to him than that.
For relief work,
you use only a round burin.
He's devoted to his craft.
Achtung! I used to engrave
champions' names on sports trophies.
Engraving victors' names
is work that calls for self-denial.
- That's defeatism, Khobotov.
- That's life.
One man wins trophies;
another engraves his name on them.
I don't know about self-denial, Lyova.
It doesn't call for subtlety.
You do it with a pointed burin.
That's a healthy outlook.
Exactly. Craftsmen don't philosophize.
- What about the gravediggers in Hamlet?
- Craftsmen.
Would you believe it? We had one
abandoned here recently too,
but they never caught who did it.
She's been off sick three days.
Pulled from the competition.
The Labor Reserves club.
Svetlana. Master of Sport.
A wonderful backstroke swimmer.
You see, at last this household
has acquired a real man.
My Savva is a treasure.
I'm very happy.
A wonderful evening.
So fascinating.
I still want you to understand.
I understand. I understand it all...
I feel alive again.
C'est magnifique.
Au revoir.
Don't even try without a scraper
and a graver. They're essential.
Darling, he's obsessed.
That's his charm.
I'll explain where
der Hund begraben ist...
where the problem lies.
I understand, colleague.
I understand it all.
Oh, really now!
Lev Yevgenyevich, stay strong.
I respect you. I admire you.
You were magnificent tonight.
Take care of yourself, dear man.
What do you mean?
Well, mein Freunde...
- Au revoir.
- Auf Wiedersehen.
Goodbye. Au revoir.
Goodbye. Auf Wiedersehen.
- My humblest respects.
- Savva! Lyovushka! Savva!
Such elevated, elevated relations.

issues.justification: The candidate contains roughly 300 lines of unrelated dialogue from the whole film script (Camões, Villon, Rimbaud, the Rosa Munda song, Orloviches, etc.) in place of a single exclamation. This is a massive addition and the segment's actual line appears only at the very end, so the item fails as a subtitle.

The stretched sibilant of 'выс-с-сокие' and its ironic emphasis are not rendered. The English 'elevated... elevated' repetition conveys the pompous tone but not the drawn-out stammer that the reference captures with 'e-v-volved'.

items.source: Живут не для радости, а для совести
items.reference: You don't live to be happy, you live to do your duty.

general.text: Данная максима вскрывает солдатский фатализм, практическую логику и бытовую прямоту Саввы Игнатьевича. Уникальность этой фразы в том, что она обнажает главный абсурд «заботы» Маргариты Павловны и Саввы: лишение Хоботова свободы и права на личное счастье подается ими как исполнение высшего морального долга.

items.candidate: We live by conscience, not for pleasure.

issues.justification: 'We live by conscience' turns the impersonal aphoristic maxim into a self-description and uses 'by' where 'for' is more idiomatic. The blunt soldierly fatalism of the source and the duty framing that exposes the 'care' as moral coercion are weakened, though the core meaning about conscience over happiness survives.

items.reference: For the record: I am not the one who suggested it!

general.text: Моментальный ответ Велюрова на предложение выпить фиксирует его лицемерное, но обаятельное позерство. Эта фраза вошла в язык как идеальная формула снятия с себя ответственности человеком, который страстно желает поддаться искушению.

items.candidate: Mind you, that was your suggestion.

issues.justification: The source is a self-disclaiming formula ('не я это предложил!'), which the analysis identifies as the meme's key feature. 'that was your suggestion' shifts the responsibility onto the listener as an accusation, so the speaker's self-exculpating formula and its comic hypocrisy are lost.

general.text: Это хлесткое восклицание подчеркивает властный, императивный характер Маргариты Павловны, привыкшей раздавать приговоры. Комический эффект достигается за счет абсурдного использования нейтрального профессионального термина в качестве громкого домашнего ругательства.

eng.nb: using literal standalone nouns (like "Culinarian!" or "Chef!"), which don't sound natural in English for this context.

issues.justification: 'The cook!' is the literal standalone noun the analysis warns against. In English it carries no insult, so the comic effect of a neutral professional term used as a household put-down is lost. The line does not make sense as a reproach.

general.text: Слово является отличным примером характерного для фильма «иноязычия как культурной игры». Использование немецкого словечка маркирует типаж Саввы как фронтовика-ремесленника и одновременно работает как комедийный знак его автоматической готовности подчиняться командам жены.

eng.nb: translating the word from German into English, which ruins the character's specific linguistic quirk.

issues.justification: The exclamation mark of 'Натюрлих!' is replaced with a period. This flattens the eager, reflexive obedience that the analysis ties to Savva's character, so the line reads as calmer than the source.

items.source: Резать к чёртовой матери, не дожидаясь перитонитов!
items.reference: Cut it the hell out, don't wait for peritonitis!

general.text: Эта реплика представляет собой пик медицинского фарса в картине. Ее ценность заключается в резком словесном контрасте: тонкие душевные терзания Хоботова грубо обрываются радикальным хирургическим приговором, который оформляет его статус беспомощного пленника ситуации.

items.candidate:
Cut the damned thing out.
Don't wait for peritonitis.

issues.justification: 'the damned thing' is a weaker and vaguer intensifier than the idiomatic 'к чёртовой матери' (reference: 'the hell out'). The sharp, colloquial impatience of the surgeon's order is somewhat diminished.

general.text: Регулярно повторяемая формула, служащая инструментом психологического подавления. Через эту реплику Маргарита Павловна постоянно утверждает свою властную позицию, обесценивая любые попытки бывшего мужа вырваться из-под опеки и выставляя его незрелым ребенком.

items.source: Это мой крест!!! И нести его мне!
items.reference: This is my cross to bear! And mine alone!

general.text: Блестящий образец манипулятивного поведения, где домашняя тирания маскируется под великое самопожертвование. Этот пассаж особенно силен тем, что Маргарита Павловна гиперболизирует свои мнимые страдания прямо на глазах у Людочки, чтобы запугать ее и сохранить абсолютный контроль над жизнью Хоботова.

eng.nb: translating literally as "This is my cross!", which improperly splits the English fixed idiom "a cross to bear".

items.candidate:
He's my cross to bear!
I'll bear him.

issues.justification: The grandiose self-pity of 'И нести его мне!' is flattened into 'I'll bear him.' The exclusive, theatrical emphasis of 'And mine alone!' is lost, and the second line reads as bland, though the idiom 'cross to bear' is correctly kept.

items.source: Я вся такая несуразная… вся угловатая такая… такая противоречивая вся
items.reference: I am so utterly awkward... just all sharp edges... so entirely contradictory!

general.text: Эта самохарактеристика стала классическим мемом, великолепно фиксирующим узнаваемый женский типаж. В ней метко высмеивается манерность, кокетливая неуверенность и наигранная психологическая глубина, что доказывает мастерство фильма в создании резко индивидуализированных речевых портретов.

eng.nb: translating «угловатая» literally as "angular", which sounds overly literal and confusing in English.

items.candidate:
Oh, I'm so awkward,
so terribly ungainly...
So full of contradictions!

issues.justification: The image of 'угловатая' (sharp edges) is dropped, and the three-part self-characterization collapses into 'awkward' and 'ungainly' followed by 'contradictions'. The added 'Oh' gives a coquettish tone, but the rhythmic repetition of 'вся' that builds the mannered self-portrait is lost.
